requirements.text: Build the plan in plans/account-erasure/: read plan.md, adr/ and spec/ first, then implement every step in plan.md in order.
Done when every step's done condition holds and npm test passes.

Rules: - KISS, YAGNI: Implement only what the ADRs and specs describe, in short plainly named functions; remove the deletedAt code the plan retires and add no options or extension points it doesn't ask for. - Gall: Get step 1's thin path (erase the account record, strip invoices, audit entry) passing end to end before extending to the other stores. - Boy Scout: Tidy code you touch in src/accounts.js, src/erasure.js, src/jobs.js and src/server.js; note problems outside the plan's scope rather than fixing them. - Testing Pyramid: For each step, write the failing test in test/erasure.test.js (or a jobs test) from its done condition first, then make it pass with the smallest change against the real in-memory db; no mocks. - Erasure window: Account deletion must erase personal data from every store, not flag it; no deletedAt left behind. - Copies count: Cover sessions, analytics events, support tickets, the newsletter subscriber and the audit log's invoice.issued userId, not just db.users. - Invoice retention: Every erased account's invoice keeps its id, issuedAt, lines, total, billing name, address and taxId until 7 years after issuedAt. - Invoice minimisation: Strip billing.email, billing.phone and userId from each retained invoice on erasure. - Audit erasure: Write account.erased and invoice.purged entries with kinds, time and rule only; assert in tests that no erased value appears in them.
